Rishi —

Saw the forwarded invite and dug into it with Mina. Quick summary:
- Anna's original .ics uses a TZID of "America/New_York" and a Google Meet link. When Gmail forwards the message as an inline forwarded .ics, some clients (Outlook desktop, some older calendar parsers) treat the DTSTART as a "floating" time (no TZID) and interpret it in the local calendar's timezone. That explains why it showed as 17:00 for me (BST) instead of 16:00 BST — daylight savings mapping plus floating interpretation caused a +1 hour drift.
- Mina in Mumbai sees 20:30 because her client converted without the proper DST offset.

Actionable fixes I recommend:
1) Re-issue a new invite with DTSTART specified in UTC (e.g., 2027-05-31T15:00:00Z) and explicit TZID blocks, or create the event from Google Calendar and add participants by email so Google keeps the timezone mapping.
2) Include the explicit wall-clock times for common regions in the body (e.g., 11:00 AM EDT / 16:00 BST / 20:30 IST) so attendees can double-check.
3) For APAC participants, consider offering a second slot or recording.

I've created a recreated-invite-utc.ics that sets the event in UTC and tested importing into Outlook and Apple Calendar — it resolved the floating interpretation. Attaching it here.

Attached: recreated-invite-utc.ics (text/calendar)
